strings.meta.og_title: Hire AI agents. Get the work done.
strings.ld.description: Owners and managers hand routine work, such as sales follow-up, customer replies, late invoices and a weekly summary, to AI agents that run it as Flows. A person approves every result before it goes out. Maskin is open source under Apache 2.0, and technical teams can run it on their own infrastructure or use the managed service.
strings.meta.title: Maskin: hire AI agents and get the work done
strings.ld.feature1: MCP-native — drive the workspace from Claude Code or Claude Desktop
strings.ld.feature2: Shared workspace for humans and AI agents
strings.ld.feature4: For You, Flows, chat and Items
strings.ld.feature5: Agents run on Claude by default; Enterprise teams can bring their own Claude subscription, API key or model endpoint
strings.ld.feature7: Open source repo for technical teams to run on their own infrastructure, or managed hosting
strings.ld.faq1.q: Do we need to be technical?
strings.ld.faq1.a: No. You explain the job in plain words. The Maskin Team does the setup.
strings.ld.faq2.q: What if it gets something wrong?
strings.ld.faq2.a: You set how much each agent can do alone. Agents with read and write access to Slack or LinkedIn send directly by default, and you can set any agent to ask first, so a person approves the exact text before it goes out, or to be blocked. Agents with read-only access cannot send.
strings.ld.faq3.a: No. A chatbot answers questions. A digital employee holds a job, owns its outcome and runs it inside a Flow.
strings.ld.faq4.a: Prices are per user, in kroner and excluding VAT, billed monthly. Free covers up to 3 users, and every new customer also gets a free 60 minute onboarding and setup session. The current prices are in the pricing section above.
strings.ld.faq5.q: How does this compare to Productboard or roadmap tools?
strings.ld.faq5.a: Productboard is built to collect feedback and show roadmaps. Maskin keeps the customer signal, the decision and the result in one record, and it has no customer portal or roadmap views.
strings.ld.faq6.q: What happened to loops and objects?
strings.ld.faq6.a: Flows were earlier called loops, and Items were earlier called objects. They are the same thing with a new name.
strings.hero.headline:
Hire AI agents.
Get the work done.
strings.hero.sub1: Your team spends the week on quotes, invoices, customer emails and reports.
strings.hero.sub2: More people is slow and costly. A chatbot only answers questions, so someone still does the work.
strings.hero.sub3: Hire digital employees for specific jobs, like sales follow-up to quiet leads. They are accountable and work towards outcomes inside Flows, the workflows of your business.
strings.proof.text: The Maskin Team runs its own sales follow-up, marketing and product work with AI agents, every day. People make the calls.
strings.method.title: Hire digital employees for specific jobs.
strings.method.1.title: Hire
strings.method.1.body: Tell the Maskin Team, on a short call, which job eats the most time. That job is your first hire.
strings.method.2.title: Brief
strings.method.2.body: Explain the job in plain words. The Maskin Team sets the agent up in the tools you already use.
strings.method.3.title: Run
strings.method.3.body: The digital employee runs the job as a Flow in the tools you already use. Results and the few questions only you can answer show up in For You, the one place a person is called in.
strings.parts.title: For You, Flows, Chat, Items.
strings.parts.1.title: For You
strings.parts.1.body: The place your digital employees report back: results to read, questions only you can answer.
strings.parts.2.title: Flows
strings.parts.2.body: The repeating jobs that run underneath, from a signal in to a result out. For example, a support Flow reads a ticket, drafts the answer and stops for your yes.
strings.parts.3.title: Chat
strings.parts.3.body: Talk to an agent that already knows your work and your Items. Ask why it did something, or change what it does next. That is the difference from a general chatbot, which starts from nothing every time.
strings.parts.4.title: Items
strings.parts.4.body: The shared record every Flow reads and writes. One example: an insight becomes a bet, the bet becomes a task, and all three sit in one place.
strings.jobs.title: The jobs that eat the week.
strings.jobs.1.line: A digital employee owns sales follow-up to quiet leads inside a Flow: it spots who went quiet and writes the next message.
strings.jobs.2.line: A digital employee owns customer replies inside a Flow: it reads incoming customer messages and writes a useful reply.
strings.jobs.3.line: A digital employee owns late invoice follow-up inside a Flow: it finds overdue invoices and writes each customer a polite reminder.
strings.jobs.4.line: A digital employee owns weekly summaries inside a Flow: every Monday, it lists what came in, what is overdue and what needs a decision.
strings.jobs.5.line: A digital employee owns research inside a Flow: it answers a question with a short written summary of the findings.
strings.example.title: What a Monday looks like.
strings.example.sub: An example, not a real customer: chasing late invoices.
strings.example.1.line: The agent opens your accounting tool and lists the 6 invoices that are overdue.
strings.example.2.line: It writes a polite reminder for each, in your wording.
strings.example.3.line: It asks: “Send these 6 reminders?” You say yes to 5 and fix 1.
strings.example.after: You spent two minutes. The agent did the rest.
strings.charge.title: Nothing goes out without your yes.
strings.charge.sub: Nothing is sent to a customer, supplier or your accountant without a yes from a person you choose.

strings.tech.title: Open source, and yours to run.
strings.tech.1: Open source. Apache 2.0. Every line is on GitHub.
strings.tech.2: Run it yourself. Technical teams can run the open-source version on their own infrastructure, or use the managed version. Self-hosted AI workspace. Comparing options? See the self-hosted AI agents landscape for 2026.
strings.tech.3: Runs on Claude. Agents run on Claude by default. Enterprise teams can bring their own Claude subscription, API key or model endpoint, with no markup on AI spend.
strings.tech.4: Flows and the marketplace. Build your own Flows, or start from a listing in the marketplace, such as the product discovery listing that turns customer signal into shipped bets. New to the vocabulary? Read the concepts.
strings.tech.5: Agent-readable. Agents drive every Item through the MCP tools, load agent skills, and read an LLM wiki before they answer.
strings.tech.6: Free onboarding. The Maskin Team sets up your first Flow with you, live. Book a free 60 minute onboarding.

strings.extra.faq_copilot_html:
How does this compare to Copilot?
A general AI assistant helps a person with a task they bring to it. Maskin hires a digital employee that holds a named job and owns the outcome, running as a Flow across the tools the business already uses.
